key_insight: A generative-design and consensus-GNN pipeline identified four DFT-validated bimetallic HER candidates with near-thermoneutral hydrogen binding: Pd5Au, Pt5Rh, Cu5Pt3, and Pd13Ru3.
engineering_relevance: The workflow focuses costly DFT validation on promising alloy structures and stoichiometries beyond those represented in the training database.
method: Fine-tune MatterGen on adsorption-labelled bulk alloys to generate novel bimetallic candidates targeting near-zero hydrogen adsorption energy.
Use MatterSim to screen facet stability and relax hydrogen-decorated slabs at high-symmetry adsorption sites.
Combine MEGNet–ALIGNN consensus with MatterSim energy-difference checks, then validate shortlisted alloys using DFT and phonons.
evidence_signal: Of eight DFT-tested alloys, four met the thermoneutral hydrogen-binding window; phonon calculations indicated dynamic stability for all eight.
watch_item: Computed hydrogen binding and dynamic stability do not establish practical HER performance or earth abundance; experimental validation is needed, and all four highlighted candidates contain precious metals.
paper_title: Generative Design and Graph Neural Network Screening of Novel Bimetallic Alloy Catalysts for the Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
